title: UI capture + privacy-masked screenshot workflow for onboarding assets
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Our onboarding and quickstart docs rely heavily on product screenshots. Manual screenshot creation is slow, inconsistent in branding (margins, colors, overlays), and error-prone for PII/localization exposure. We need an automated, reproducible capture pipeline that produces brand-consistent, privacy-safe screenshots across locales and retina/low-DPI variants and integrates with our docs and release flow.

Goals:
- Define UX and visual rules for cropping, padding, and contrast that preserve readability and branding.
- Specify a masking/redaction approach for dynamic user data (emails, API keys, tokens) that is deterministic and reviewable.
- Create a localization-safe process so strings in screenshots can be replaced or flagged for translation review.
- Produce clear handoff artifacts for engineering to implement capture scripts and for docs to reference auto-generated images.

Constraints/Non-goals:
- We are not building a full screenshot orchestration service in design; this ticket defines assets, specs, and validation artifacts.
- High-fidelity image optimization (format micro-optimizations) belongs to ENG-4330.

Proposed approach:
1) Capture spec: visual grid with three viewport sizes (desktop 1440 x auto, tablet 1024 x auto, mobile 428 x auto). Centered frame with 48px outer padding in brand color background, 24px inner safe zone for UI elements.
2) Redaction rules: use two-level masking tokens: (a) structural mask replaces single-line user content with deterministic placeholders (e.g., "redwood_user_****") preserving character width for layout, (b) full-block mask for sensitive widgets (API keys / tokens) replaced by a blurred pill with clear label "REDACTED" for reviewers. Provide regex-based rules for common PII patterns.
3) Localization safe layers: separate UI text from visual layer using layer annotations in Figma and metadata in capture JSON. Provide fallback rules for long translations (ellipsis, wrap) and style overrides for RTL.
4) Export variants: produce both "annotated" (with overlays showing redaction/type info) for internal review and "final" (no overlays) for public docs. Each variant includes locale suffix and retina indicator (@2x).
5) Review flow: automated diff images placed in review folder, plus a lightweight checklist for PM/Design to sign off before release.

Deliverables from Design:
- Figma component library: screenshot-frame, redaction overlays, annotated markers, and localized text tokens.
- Visual spec doc (this ticket) with precise pixel measurements and color tokens.
- Acceptance criteria test images (English, German, Japanese, RTL Arabic) demonstrating masks and layout.
- Hand-off README for ENG with regex rules, export naming conventions, and sample capture command examples.

Success metrics:
- Reduction of manual screenshot time by 70% for release bundles.
- Zero public screenshots with live PII in the next three releases.
- 95% first-pass signoff rate from PM/docs reviewers when using the pipeline.
